Trainable attention of one sequence (Query) over another (Key / Value)

Each Query position attends over the Key / Value sequence: softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) V per head, with learned projections W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o (torch.nn.MultiheadAttention(query, key, value), batch first). Query is [batch, query length, embed_dim]; Key and Value are [batch, key length, embed_dim] and may come from another branch with a different length (link the same layer to both for the usual memory input). The output has the Query's shape. Code export does not support it yet.

## Settings

| Group | Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Attention | Embedding Dimension | `embed_dim` | Integer | `512` | `1-65536` | The run | Feature width of Query, Key and Value. Required. |
| Attention | Attention Heads | `num_heads` | Integer | `8` | `1-4096` | The run | Number of attention heads; embed_dim must divide evenly. Required. |
| Regularization | Dropout | `dropout` | Number | `0.0` | `0.0-0.999` | The run | Dropout on the attention weights while training. |
| Advanced | Use Bias | `use_bias` | On / off | `true` |   | The run | Enable bias in the attention projections. Advanced. |
| Fine-tuning | Frozen | `frozen` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Keeps this layer's weights as they are while the rest of the model trains: no gradient step, no weight decay, no optimizer memory. Use it on layers that start from a weights file (fine-tuning), then turn it off to train them too. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Where it runs

| Where | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| Training (the compiled model) | Yes, as a layer of the model: compiled as a trainable two-input attention layer (Query over Key / Value) in the graph runtime |

The node runs on the device chosen for the run (CPU or a GPU); a node does not fix a device.

## Usage

```text
Each Query position attends over the Key / Value sequence (softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) V per head) with learned projections, as torch.nn.MultiheadAttention(query, key, value) with batch_first. Query, Key and Value usually come from different graph branches; the output has the Query's shape.
```

## Tips

- Link the same layer to Key and Value for the usual encoder memory input.
- Query and Key may have different lengths; Key and Value must match.
- Code export does not support Cross Attention yet.

## How it computes

Every position of the **Query** sequence attends over the **Key / Value**
sequence and comes back as a weighted mix of the values. It is
`torch.nn.MultiheadAttention(query, key, value)` with `batch_first=True`:

```text
softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) V   per head,  Q = query W_q,  K = key W_k,  V = value W_v,  out = concat(heads) W_o
```

Query, Key and Value all have the width `embed_dim`; the Query and Key
lengths may differ, and the output has the Query's shape. Compile checks
that each input is connected and is a `[length, embed_dim]` sequence, and
that Key and Value have the same length.

## Wire it

The inputs come from different branches of the graph. For example, split one
sequence into a "question" part and a "context" part:

```text
Data [8, 4] -> Split (split_size 2) --Output 1 [2, 4]--> Cross Attention.Query
                                    --Output 2 [6, 4]--> Cross Attention.Key
                                                     \-> Cross Attention.Value
Cross Attention [2, 4] -> Flatten -> Dense -> loss
```

or give each branch its own encoder layers (Embedding, Transformer Encoder,
Dense) before the attention. With token ids, split the ids and give each
part its own Embedding. For attention of a sequence over itself use
[Multi-Head Attention](multi-head-attention.md).

## Limits

- Training runs in the graph runtime: the three inputs are matched by pin,
  and the gradient goes back to each input (Key and Value linked from the
  same layer add up), as in PyTorch. Forward output, input gradient and
  every parameter gradient are checked against PyTorch, with Key and Value
  from one branch and from separate branches.
- There is no attention mask: every Query position sees every Key position.
- The code exports refuse it and say so; train it in Studio.
